e.etymology: From the Basque word eder, beautiful or handsome, and well used across Latin America. Eder is also a minor Old Testament name, Hebrew for flock.
A modern American name that joins the Ry- of Ryan and Riley to the -lin ending of Kaylin and Jaylin.
From Arabic minha, a gift or grant, used by Muslim families and especially South Asian ones. Minha is also a separate Korean name whose meaning depends on the characters chosen.
e.note: In Portuguese, minha is the everyday word for my.

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Natalie, the French form of Latin Natalia, from natale Domini, the birthday of the Lord, a name first given to girls born at Christmas.
namesakes: Natalee Holloway (Alabama teen who disappeared in Aruba in 2005)

assoc.t: Natalee Holloway, US teen who vanished in Aruba in 2005

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Cameron, a Scottish clan name from Gaelic cam sron, crooked nose.
From Arabic Fatima, one who abstains, also read as one who weans a child. It honors Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad, and is among the most widely given names in the Muslim world.
namesakes: Fatimah bint Muhammad (daughter of the Prophet Muhammad)

assoc.t: Fatima, Catholic pilgrimage shrine in Portugal

e.etymology: From the Scottish place and surname Irvine, probably from Celtic words for fresh and river. American Jewish families once used it to anglicize Israel.
namesakes: Irving Berlin (composer of White Christmas and God Bless America)
Washington Irving (author of The Legend of Sleepy Hollow)

assoc.t: Irving, Texas, a large Dallas suburb

e.etymology: From Arabic Husayn, a diminutive of Hasan, good or handsome. It honors Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, who is especially revered by Shia Muslims.
namesakes: Husayn ibn Ali (grandson of the Prophet Muhammad)

assoc.t: Saddam Hussein, former dictator of Iraq
middle name of President Barack Hussein Obama

e.note: Many Americans connect the name first with Saddam Hussein.

e.etymology: A modern American name in the style of Javion and Davion. It also matches avion, the French word for airplane, which is avión in Spanish.

assoc.t: avion, French and Spanish word for airplane
Avión, premium tequila brand

e.etymology: A spelling of Annalee, a combination of Anna and Lee, with the -leigh ending of Ashleigh and Everleigh.
A surname used as a first name beside Payton and Grayson. Sources disagree on its root: an English name meaning son of Pay, or a Danish and North German form of Paysen, son of Paul.

assoc.t: Payson, Arizona and Payson, Utah
Payson Keeler, gymnast on TV's Make It or Break It

e.etymology: From Sanskrit shaurya, bravery or heroism, a word still in everyday use in Hindi. It is a popular modern boys' name in India.
A modern American name that puts a Z in front of Aaliyah, in line with Zariyah and Taliyah.
An African-American coinage of the late 20th century that joins Tre-, as in Trevor and Trey, to the -von of Devon and Javon.

e.meaning: great ruler, later read as ruler of the world
e.etymology: From Old Slavic Volodimer, to rule plus great or famous; the ending was later read as mir, peace or world. Vladimir the Great, prince of Kyiv, made Christianity the religion of the Rus in 988.
namesakes: Vladimir Lenin (leader of the Russian Revolution)
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (Toronto Blue Jays slugger)

assoc.t: Vladimir Putin, president of Russia

e.note: Most Americans connect the name first with Vladimir Putin.

e.etymology: Built from Jett and the -son ending of Jackson and Hudson; Jetson is also a rare English surname. Most people know it from The Jetsons, the 1960s space-age cartoon family.

assoc.t: The Jetsons, Hanna-Barbera's space-age cartoon family
Jetson, maker of e-bikes, scooters and hoverboards

e.etymology: A spelling of Isabel, the medieval Spanish form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. This spelling was common in America around 1900 and is used in Germany and Scandinavia.
A modern American name that joins the Bray- of Brayden to the -son of Grayson and Jason. Brayson also exists as a rare surname.
An English surname from places in Cumbria and Northumberland, from Old Norse kaupland, bought land.
namesakes: Misty Copeland (American Ballet Theatre principal dancer)

e.etymology: A respelling of Kehlani, the name of the R&B singer, which is itself a variant of the Hawaiian names Kalani, the heavens, and Kailani, sea and sky.

assoc.t: Kehlani, R&B singer (the usual spelling)

e.etymology: Taken from the rock band Van Halen, whose Dutch surname means from Halen, a town in Belgium. It also sits easily beside Jalen and Hayden.

assoc.t: Van Halen, the rock band of Eddie Van Halen

e.etymology: The English word, from Greek rhythmos, measured flow or movement. It joins Lyric, Melody and Harmony among musical word names.
In the United States a modern name close in sound to Zara, Kyra and Myra. Zyra is also recorded as an Albanian girls' name.

assoc.t: Zyra, plant-mage champion in League of Legends

e.etymology: Brought into American use by tap dancer Savion Glover, born in 1973. It fits with Javion and Davion, and Savyon is also a Hebrew name taken from a yellow wildflower.
namesakes: Savion Glover (Tony-winning tap dancer and choreographer)

e.etymology: A place name and surname meaning Charles's town. Charleston, South Carolina, was founded in 1670 as Charles Town in honor of King Charles II of England.

assoc.t: Charleston, South Carolina
the Charleston, 1920s dance craze
Charleston, capital of West Virginia

e.etymology: From the English adjective golden, also an English and Irish surname. It was given as a first name in the late 1800s and has returned with other color and word names.

assoc.t: Golden, 2025 hit song from KPop Demon Hunters
Golden, Colorado, home of Coors

e.etymology: A Spanish-language Biblical name, usually taken as a form of Isaí, the Spanish Bible's name for Jesse, father of King David, or as a short form of Esaías (Isaiah).
namesakes: Esai Morales (actor in La Bamba and NYPD Blue)

e.etymology: A spelling of Talia, Hebrew for dew of God, from tal, dew, and Yah. Talia is also used as a short form of Natalia.
A double-m spelling of Emerson, an English surname meaning son of Emery, a Norman name of Germanic origin. The extra m lines it up with Emma and Emmy, and this spelling goes mostly to girls.

assoc.t: Ralph Waldo Emerson, essayist and poet (one m)

e.etymology: From Old Irish Aife, probably from aoibh, beauty or radiance. In Irish legend Aoife is a warrior woman who fights the hero Cu Chulainn, and the name is a long-time favorite in Ireland.
e.note: Most Americans cannot guess the sound from the spelling; it is said EE-fuh.

e.meaning: June, the month named for the goddess Juno
e.etymology: A pet form of June, the month named for the Roman goddess Juno, and now of Juniper too. It was also an old nickname for Junius and for boys called Junior.
namesakes: Junie B. Jones (heroine of the children's book series)

assoc.t: Junie B. Jones, children's book heroine

e.etymology: A K spelling of Colson, an English surname meaning son of Col, a medieval short form of Nicholas.
